business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Air Freight Forwarding and Cargo Aircraft Charter

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations, cantonal civil law codes, unified federal commercial registration and company law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 27 January 2009, entered into force 13 April 2010)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 25 September 2013, entered into force 13 March 2014)
Switzerland-EU Bilateral Agreements I and II, including the Agreement on Air Transport
Switzerland-EU Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/MLA, SR 955.0); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), including Articles 627 and 697j et seq.; Money Laundering Ordinance (SR 955.01); FINMA Circular 2016/07 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; SECO sanctions, embargoes and export control legislation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity card copy of each director, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport authority in the document holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague states, consular legalization by a Swiss diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and extract from the foreign commercial register of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registrar or secretary of state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague member states, Swiss consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and legalized power of attorney for the Swiss incorporation filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for the initial capital contribution (minimum CHF 100,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication confirmed by the Swiss AML gatekeeper; bank signature legalized by apostille or consular legalization where required by the Swiss bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions and embargoes, US OFAC SDN list, UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists, and Swiss domestic politically exposed persons (PEP) databases, with enhanced due diligence for PEPs and ongoing transaction monitoring under FINMA Circular 2016/07. Negative findings must be documented and cleared before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) plus the relevant cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be distinguishable, truthful and non-misleading. It may be chosen in any Swiss official language (German, French or Italian) or in English. Names in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese or Russian, must be transliterated into Roman/Latin characters for registration; non-transliterated characters are not accepted. An Aktiengesellschaft must append the legal-form suffix 'AG' when the registered articles are in German, or 'SA' when in French or Italian; alternatively the full forms 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'Société Anonyme' may be used.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Trust (when implying fiduciary or custody services)
Foundation (as a legal-form suffix for an AG)
International or Global (without actual international presence)
Name of a municipality or canton implying official public character
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial register office refuses a proposed name, the applicant receives a written refusal with legal reasons. Within 30 days of notification, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the same cantonal commercial register office or a formal administrative complaint with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority. If the refusal is sustained, an appeal may be brought to the competent cantonal administrative court and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. The preliminary name clearance may be renewed within its 180-day validity window by paying the applicable cantonal fee; if the clearance expires, a new application must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mail-forwarding or virtual-office address is not acceptable as the registered seat of a Swiss AG conducting licensed air cargo charter brokerage. The company must maintain a physical office in the municipality named in its articles of association, where management actually conducts business and where official supervision by the Federal Office of Civil Aviation, Swiss customs and AML/CFT supervisory authorities can be exercised. A serviced or co-working office with individual lockable premises and on-site administrative capacity may be accepted if the applicant submits a valid right-of-use certificate and the cantonal commercial register office approves the address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high: unannounced on-site inspections by the Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA), the Swiss Federal Customs Administration and AML/CFT supervisors are reasonably expected; annual likelihood estimated at 35% to 50% during the first three years of the air cargo charter brokerage licence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and preliminary Zefix/cantonal name search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee per cantonal fee schedule (Gebührenverordnung)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial preparation and certification of the articles of association (Statuten, minimum CHF 100,000 share capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff plus 0.1% to 0.2% of nominal capital; prevailing market benchmark for a standard AG formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign UBO/corporate documents, powers of attorney and due diligence document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign apostille authorities and Embassy of Switzerland
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule and per-document apostille fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/PEP/sanctions screening and AML/CFT risk on-boarding file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GLBA/AML compliance due-diligence benchmark; FINMA-compliant enhanced due diligence hourly rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry, official announcement in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and registered-office right-of-use verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal commercial register office and SHAB
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Swiss commercial registry fee (HRegV fee schedule) and SHAB publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss air cargo charter broker licence preliminary consultation and FOCA regulatory assessment fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA) and Federal Office for Transport
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulatory administrative tariff and aviation licensing assessment fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / societe anonyme), in particular Arts. 621 (minimum capital), 632 (paid-up capital), 640 (notarization of deed), 652 (share subscription), 698 (general assembly), 716a (non-delegable board duties), 718 (signature and Swiss residence rule), 727-731 (audit); supplemented by the Swiss Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRegG) and the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV), Arts. 20-32; publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), acting within the Swiss Commercial Register network accessible via Zefix (Central Business Name Index of Switzerland).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Act of Incorporation (Errichtungserklarung / acte constitutif) comprising the incorporation declaration, the Articles of Association (Statuten), the incorporation report (Grundungsbericht), the subscription statement, and the bank's certificate of paid-up capital; submitted as a single dossier via the e-Handelsregister electronic filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum registered share capital is CHF 100,000 (Art. 621(1) OR), of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up before entry in the Commercial Register (Art. 632(1) OR). The paid-up amount must be deposited into a blocked escrow account held in the name of the company in formation at a SIX-member Swiss bank; the bank issues an irrevocable payment confirmation (Eingabebescheinigung) attesting that the funds are at the company's free disposal and not subject to pledge, repayment agreement, or offset; the funds are released to the company upon definitive registration; non-cash contributions require an additional statutory audit report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of CH AG, having reviewed the constitutional deed and capital payment confirmation, adopts the following resolutions: (1) The subscription of 100,000 registered shares of CHF 1.00 nominal each, fully paid-in as evidenced by the bank's escrow release certificate, is ratified; the company's share capital is set at CHF 100,000. (2) The registered office is established at Zugerstrasse 12, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. (3) [Shareholder 1] is elected Chairman of the Board; [Shareholder 2] is appointed as member; [Name] is appointed Managing Director/Broker in charge with sole signature authority for corporate filings and banking operations. (4) The appointed auditor and the corporation's compliance officer are confirmed according to Art. 727 et seq. CO and AML obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation notarization of deed and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notariat des Kantons Zug (Cantonal Notary Public Office, Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear in person before a notary public of the Canton of Zug with original valid passports or identity cards. The notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of each founder, confirms the uniqueness and lawfulness of the corporate name against the Zefix name index, and authenticates the deed of incorporation together with the final Articles of Association. The deed must be executed in German and must state the purpose (air cargo charter brokerage and freight forwarding under ISIC 5229), the share capital, the registered office in the municipality of Zug, and the board composition. The notary also verifies that at least one individual with individual signature authority is resident in Switzerland as required by Art. 718 CO.
required_dossiers: Original valid passports or ID cards of all founders/shareholders
Certificate of name approval from the Zefix commercial name reservation system
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten) including purpose clause for air cargo charter brokerage
Notarized power of attorney if a representative acts for any founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a deficiency in the name, purpose, or capital schedule, the Articles are amended and re-executed by the founders; if the name is rejected, a new name reservation is submitted through Zefix without reopening the notarization if only clerical fields change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and bank payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank chosen by the founders (SIX member, e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A blocked escrow account is opened in the name of 'CH AG in formation' with the target registered office address. At least CHF 50,000 is remitted by wire transfer by the founders from untainted bank accounts. The bank performs know-your-client and source-of-funds checks and issues the statutory payment certificate (Eingabebescheinigung) addressed to the notary and the Commercial Register Office, confirming that the amount has been credited and is irrevocably at the free disposal of the company. The certificate must be dated within a short period before filing, normally less than 30 days.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized incorporation deed
Founders' identification and beneficial ownership declaration forms
Business plan and proof of source of funds for enhanced due diligence
Bank account opening questionnaire and wire transfer reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening for AML reasons, the founders substitute another SIX-member bank and re-issue the payment confirmation; this substitution does not require re-notarization, provided the corporate name and deed remain unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Commercial Register and SHAB publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (electronic filing via e-Handelsregister portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or licensed lawyer files the complete dossier electronically through the e-Handelsregister portal. The filing must contain the notarized deed, the Articles of Association, the incorporation report signed by founders, the bank payment certificate, and written acceptances of office signed by each director and auditor. The Commercial Register Office reviews formal and substantive legality, verifies capital payment and the Swiss-residence rule under Art. 718 CO, and upon approval orders registration and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB). The company acquires legal personality on publication of the entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank payment confirmation (Eingabebescheinigung)
Incorporation report (Grundungsbericht) signed by all founders
Written declarations of acceptance by directors and auditor
Audit report for any non-cash contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a deficiency notice (Mangelruege) from the Commercial Register Office, the notary or counsel cures the defect within the imposed deadline, usually 30 days. A formal refusal can be appealed to the Cantonal Administrative Court of Zug (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of receipt; no additional registry fee applies to a corrective re-filing caused by the Office's query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal tax (VAT), UID, and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and the Compensation Office of the Canton of Zug (AHV-Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Commercial Register extract, the board applies for VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration using the official form, even where the annual turnover is below the CHF 100,000 exemption threshold, so as to allow input VAT recovery and future invoice compliance. The company automatically receives its Enterprise Identification Number (UID). The board simultaneously registers the employer with the AHV-Ausgleichskasse for social security (AHV/IV/EO) payroll contributions and appoints an accident insurer (Suva or private carrier) as required by the Federal Accident Insurance Act.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (newly issued)
Articles of Association
Federal VAT registration form
Beneficial ownership and UBO schedule
Payroll and employer registration declaration for AHV/IV/EO
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT registration is delayed or queried, the board files a supplementary statement within 60 days; where late registration triggers default interest, the company may apply for interest waiver upon showing good faith. Social security registration is deemed effective from the date the payroll activity begins.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate retrieval, corporate books, and operational bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug and the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board or its counsel collects the certified extract evidencing the SHAB publication and legal personality. The board then adopts organizational minutes, opens the shareholder register (Aktienbuch), records the share transfers and issues share certificates, seals the corporate minute book, and designates the registered office as the place of administration. The operational corporate bank account is opened using the certified extract and the board resolution, enabling the intended SWIFT wire and Fedwire payment rails for cargo charter settlement.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract after publication
Board organizational minutes and signature specimen cards
Shareholder register (Aktienbuch)
Registered office lease agreement
Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the operational bank applies enhanced due diligence due to the cargo-broker or crypto-adjacent profile, the company supplies a certified statement of sources of funds and a transactional flow chart prepared by a Swiss trustee; if the extract contains any typographical error, the Commercial Register Office issues a free rectification entry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA/BAZL) - Aviation Security Division; Swiss Federal Customs Administration (FOCBS/EZV) for Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) status; Municipality of Zug for the local business permit (Betriebsbewilligung).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviation Security Regulated Agent (RA) Certification under the Swiss implementing provisions of EU Regulation 2015/1998 (incorporated into Annex 9 of the Swiss Aircraft Act); separate FOCBS AEO-C certificate for customs simplification; an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) is not required for a pure charter broker that does not operate aircraft.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) for national coordination; Cantonal Department of the Environment of Zug (Amt fuer Umweltschutz des Kantons Zug) as the executing authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Administrative registration category, exempt from a full EIA report, for a pure office-based brokerage activity; a preliminary Category B assessment under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVP-VPV) becomes mandatory if the company adds warehousing, cargo consolidation, or a transhipment terminal exceeding the Annex I thresholds (e.g., logistics warehouse floor area).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: any drainage from washing or cargo treatment stations must connect to the municipal sewer in compliance with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) and cantonal limits (COD < 200 mg/L, BOD5 < 20 mg/L, pH 6.5-9.0). Air emissions: solvent-based cargo treatment facilities are subject to the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) Annex 3 with VOC concentration limit of 150 mg C/m3 at a mass flow above 1 kg/h; fugitive VOC emissions from stored packaged dangerous goods must be controlled and reported. Waste: hazardous cargo waste must be tracked under the Swiss Waste Ordinance (VVEA) and stored no longer than six months prior to licensed disposal.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Feuerpolizei des Kantons Zug under the cantonal Fire Ordinance for the registered office and any storage mezzanine; structural load certificate by a licensed engineer for any racking or aircraft cargo consolidation platform; occupational safety validation by Suva or the accident insurer under Art. 82 UVG covering workplace risk assessment, fire evacuation plan, and forklift traffic management; for the office-only brokerage model, a municipal business permit (Betriebsbewilligung) and a rescue plan approval suffice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA) - Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC) / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni (AFC); Headquarters: Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern, Switzerland. Official e-services portal: https://www.esty.admin.ch; Business Identifier registry: https://www.uid.admin.ch; VAT e-filing is performed through the SFTA's E-Steuererklärung MWST online platform. Cantonal tax administrations administer cantonal and communal corporate taxes, while the SFTA administers federal corporate tax, VAT, withholding tax and stamp duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP for a foreign-owned Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) Execute notarial deed of incorporation under Art. 629 ff. Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) with minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 and deposit of at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) with a Swiss bank; (2) File the application for entry with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); upon entry, the Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX) automatically issues the Swiss Business Identifier (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer UID / IDE / IDI) in the format CHE-116.412.235, which serves as the statutory corporate TIN for all federal and cantonal tax purposes; (3) Where the AG's worldwide annual turnover from taxable supplies reaches or is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, or where voluntary VAT registration is sought, submit the VAT registration questionnaire (Fragebogen zur MWST-Registrierung) electronically to the SFTA within 30 days of the commencement of VAT liability (Art. 68(1) MWSTG); the SFTA issues the VAT number by appending the suffix 'MWST' to the UID (e.g., CHE-116.412.235 MWST); (4) VAT registration is generally non-retroactive; foreign shareholders may own 100% of the AG without a Swiss fiscal representative, but a Swiss registered office and a Swiss bank confirmation of the capital deposit are mandatory; (5) For export operations, complete the customs declarant registration in the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (BAZG/OFDF) electronic declaration system (e-dec / Passar-NCTS) using the UID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (opaque Aktiengesellschaft under Art. 620-763 OR); no pass-through or tax-transparent status is available; the Swiss tax profile combines Entity_Level_Taxation with Territorial_Scope elements, since foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate and their related income are exempt from Swiss corporate income tax with progression (Art. 52(1) DBG / Art. 21(3) StHG); the AG is subject to unlimited Swiss tax liability on its worldwide income otherwise, with participation relief and treaty-based residence benefits as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no check-the-box or hybrid entity election; legal-form classification follows the Code of Obligations and is mandatory for an AG. Available elections and rulings: (i) Tax-privileged holding company and mixed/administrative company status per Art. 69-75 StHG and Art. 28-29 DBG, elected through the annual tax return and verified by SFTA/cantonal qualification certificates, providing participation exemption and cantonal profit-tax relief on non-Swiss source income; (ii) Principal-company ruling in cantons such as Zug, Zurich and Geneva for foreign-group centralization of cross-border procurement and charter-brokerage functions; (iii) Federal and cantonal patent box and additional R&D deduction elections under the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF/USTAF); (iv) Participation deduction (Beteiligungsabzug, Art. 69 DBG / Art. 28 StHG) applied by election in the tax assessment subject to the 10% minimum participation and qualifying-dividend thresholds; (v) VAT group registration election (Art. 11 MWSTG) for Swiss entities that are financially integrated at the 100% direct or indirect ownership level; (vi) OECD BEPS hybrid-mismatch alignment is achieved through treaty rules and domestic substance requirements rather than through any domestic transparent-entity election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / MWST / TVA / IVA) under the Swiss Federal Value Added Tax Act of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG; SR 641.20)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 per calendar year of worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10(1)(a) MWSTG) for persons established in Switzerland. A resident Swiss AG must register when this threshold is reached; the turnover of structurally related enterprises is aggregated for threshold purposes (Art. 10(3) MWSTG). Non-established suppliers supplying services taxable in Switzerland are liable regardless of turnover, subject to the reverse-charge relief in Art. 10(2)(c) MWSTG where the Swiss recipient is itself a VAT-liable business. Voluntary registration is permitted from the start of the business activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), no digital stamping, no pre-clearance API and no government authorization for invoice issuance. Invoices may be issued on paper or electronically. Electronic invoices qualify as input-VAT vouchers only if they comply with the SESTA (Swiss Standard for Electronic Invoicing for Tax Purposes) XML structure, containing the mandatory SFTA data fields: supplier and recipient UID-MWST numbers, invoice number and date, description of the supply, quantity, net amount, VAT rate and VAT amount (Art. 26(2) MWSTG). Recognized formats include the SESTA-compliant Swiss QR-bill / e-bill with embedded UID-MWST metadata. All VAT-relevant documents must be retained for 10 years (Art. 87 MWSTG). VAT returns are filed electronically with the SFTA via the E-Steuererklärung MWST portal, generally on a quarterly basis, and are due within 60 days after the end of the reporting period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Swiss VAT law exempts exports of goods and qualifying cross-border services with full input VAT deduction, producing an effective 0% rate. Eligibility for the ISIC 5229/02 air-cargo charter broker rests on three statutory pillars: (i) Export of goods under Art. 23(1)(1) MWSTG, where the foreign recipient obtains the power of disposal and the goods are transported out of Swiss customs territory, evidenced by a Swiss customs export declaration; (ii) Services related to export goods supplied to recipients abroad under Art. 23(2)(2) MWSTG; and (iii) Transport services and related services in cross-border traffic, including international air freight carriage and the agency/brokerage commission of an air-cargo charter broker, zero-rated under Art. 23(2)(4) MWSTG, provided the underlying carriage crosses the Swiss customs frontier and the air waybill proves the international routing. The commission for arranging an international cargo aircraft charter therefore qualifies for 0% VAT where CH_AG contracts as broker or as principal for an international charter movement; any purely domestic Swiss carriage or brokerage related only to domestic transport remains taxable at the standard 8.1% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / e-dec declaration in the Swiss customs system) including the certified export certificate (Ausfuhrschein / formulaire d'exportation) evidencing legal export from Swiss customs territory.

Outward Air Waybill (Master and House AWB) transmitted via CASS or directly by the carrier, showing the Swiss origin airport (ZRH/GVA/BSL), the foreign destination, cargo description, and the consignee abroad.

Commercial invoice (original) issued by CH_AG with the explicit annotation '0% MWST - Ausfuhr (Art. 23 Abs. 1 MWSTG)' or 'International air cargo charter brokerage - Art. 23 Abs. 2 Ziff. 4 MWSTG', including the UID-MWST number of CH_AG and the customer's tax identification.

Inward remittance certificate or bank statement (Kontoauszug / Beleg) evidencing receipt of the export consideration from the foreign customer or charterer, aligned with the 180-day cash-settlement benchmark.

Air cargo charter brokerage agreement / GSA (General Sales Agency) or booking confirmation together with the underlying charter party or freight contract, documenting that CH_AG acted as broker or as contracting principal, the basis of the commission, and the international route.
Cargo manifest and proof of delivery (POD) / cargo arrival notice, providing supplemental evidence of the physical departure from Switzerland and the international destination of the goods.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SFTA and the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (BAZG/OFDF) conduct cross-system reconciliation between export declarations, outbound AWB data, VAT returns and bank-inflow records under the export-refund review procedure (Art. 34 and Art. 83 MWSTG). Swiss law imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline, as the Swiss capital and foreign-exchange markets are fully liberalized (Art. 27 BV); the 180-day marker represents the conservative documentary-settlement benchmark used by the SFTA, customs auditors and banks to corroborate the receipt of genuine export consideration, and longer payment terms require contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. If the 0% export exemption is disallowed, the SFTA retroactively assesses VAT at the standard rate of 8.1% on the invoiced commission or charter fee, adds statutory default interest (Verzugszins as published annually by the SFTA), and claws back the corresponding input VAT deduction; the assessment limitation period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of tax evasion (Art. 42(4) MWSTG). Penalties: failure to keep vouchers, refusal to provide information and procedural violations attract administrative fines of up to CHF 10,000 per offence (Art. 98 MWSTG); deliberate VAT evasion attracts a fine of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 96 MWSTG); qualified evasion or intentional false certification attracts imprisonment of up to one year or a monetary penalty (Art. 97 MWSTG), with individual liability of the directors and officers of CH_AG for intent or negligence. Adverse findings may additionally trigger administrative criminal proceedings under the Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR), revocation of the customs declarant authorization, and exclusion from future export zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking and securities supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible, and there are no general exchange control restrictions on cross-border capital movements, dividend distributions, or profit remittances. However, all cross-border fund transfers are subject to Swiss Anti-Money Laundering (AMLA) due diligence, and cash or high-value transfers may be scrutinized for tax and sanctions compliance. For an air cargo charter broker with a Swiss AG, no prior central bank approval is required for profit remittances, dividends, or intercompany loans, provided the transactions are commercially justified and properly documented. The only hurdles are statutory reporting thresholds (e.g., cross-border payments exceeding CHF 100,000 require a declaration to the Swiss Customs or reporting in line with SNB statistical reporting if the company is part of the financial statistics cohort).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland does not impose any compulsory surrender, mandatory conversion, or statutory repatriation timeline on export proceeds. An exempt taxpayer or a regular Swiss AG air cargo charter broker may retain export receivables in any currency, maintain foreign currency accounts, and convert them at will. The SNB requires statistical reporting for resident companies receiving payments from abroad only when the threshold materiality criteria apply (e.g., receiving or paying in excess of CHF 50 million per year in cross-border transactions). No export proceeds need to be converted into CHF.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is rated Medium. Swiss-regulated FinTech companies holding a FINMA FinTech licence (Article 1b Banking Act) may accept public deposits up to CHF 100 million but cannot perform full commercial banking activities. Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) offering e-money accounts for Swiss companies are generally not permitted to provide Swiss IBANs or operate as banks without a Swiss banking licence or passporting arrangement (Switzerland is not an EEA member). For inbound international wire settlements and FX execution, engagement with an unlicensed offshore EMI is high-risk and may create OFAC/FINMA sanctions compliance gaps. Recommended structure: use a tier-1 Swiss bank as the primary settlement account and, if necessary, a licensed EU EMI (e.g., with Malta or Lithuania banking passport) only for non-CHF collections from non-UK/EU clients, with all client SARs processed through the Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Swiss AG with a non-Swiss ultimate beneficial owner, most major Swiss banks require at least one director or authorized signatory to appear physically in Switzerland for the initial onboarding interview and signature verification. Remote electronic identification (eID) is accepted by certain cantonal banks and FinTechs under FINMA Circular 2016/07 only for low-risk personal accounts or when a bank has an approved video-identification process and performs enhanced due diligence. For a corporate account in the air freight forwarding sector (which is prudently classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced under Swiss GWG/AML Ordinance-FINMA), a physical presence interview is effectively mandated. The corporate secretary or a Swiss-resident director with a power of attorney can sometimes attend the physical interview, but the ultimate beneficial owner must provide authenticated passport copies and confirm wire transfer instructions; several banks additionally require the UBO to attend in person either in Switzerland or at a corresponding bank branch with a personally notarized identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data mismatch between beneficial ownership, corporate purpose, and actual airplane charter transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full corporate registry extract (Handelsregisterauszug) proving the AG's legal formation, executed articles of incorporation, an organizational chart identifying all directors and shareholders, a signed declaration of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) under the Swiss association to anti-money laundering guidelines, audited or management accounts, and a detailed business narrative explaining the charter brokerage operating model with counterparty names, aircraft operator contracts, and expected transaction flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore holding company or high-sanctions-risk jurisdictions among counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide enhanced due diligence files for all offshore charter operators and aircraft lessors, including registry extracts, operating certificates (AOC/Part 129/Part 135 equivalents), proof of valid accident liability insurance (e.g., ICAO Third Party Liability), up-to-date commercial sanctions screening reports (FINMA/OFS/OFAC/EU sanctions), and an executed compliance undertaking prohibiting transactions with embargoed states or entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire transfers from third countries with unverified origin or purpose code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a transaction ledger with SWIFT message copies, invoices, charter agreements, proof of aircraft operating permits, certificate of non-availability of exchange controls, and, where applicable, the underlying charter contract showing delivery points, freight invoices, and termination clauses. Include a written confirmation that no party qualifies as a politically exposed person (PEP) or a member of a restricted list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk financial actions by proxy signatories (authorized representatives) without UBO presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of the board resolution authorizing restricted powers, a corporate signature card signed in front of the bank officer, proof that the UBO participated in the onboarding due diligence call or video conference, and a corporate AML policy requiring dual authorization for payments above CHF 50,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from a shareholder or related party are best routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (for interbank cover payments) to the Swiss bank account, using purpose code 'Equity Capital Injection' or 'Shareholder Loan'. Under Switzerland's bilateral tax treaty network and the EU-Swiss Savings Tax Agreement, the sending bank may require an International Bank Account Number (IBAN) and the Swiss IBAN starting with 'CH'. The inbound transfer should be accompanied by an executed loan agreement or subscription/contribution resolution, a statement of capital under notarial deed, and, in the case of third-party loans, a confirmation that the transaction complies with Swiss Ordinance on Financial Services (FinSA) and does not constitute a lending business requiring a license. For non-EU-USD transfers, the correspondent routing must be provided with the receiving bank's SWIFT BIC; the bank will verify the origin of funds and confirm the purpose code, which must match the corporate object of the AG (air freight charter brokering) to avoid rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for aircraft charter operations, fuel, ground handling, landing fees, insurance premia, and crew cost settlements should be executed through the following clearing rails: (1) AP.13/SWIFT MT103 for genuine commercial money transfers, always including the beneficiary bank's BIC, IBAN/USA ABA or account number, and a purpose code consistent with the invoice; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued via the Swiss bank's trade finance desk when the counterparty demands a documentary guarantee or when the air cargo broker is acting as a principal in aircraft charter transactions; (3) Fedwire for USD-denominated disbursements to US-based cargo operators, with the payment notice clearly identifying the underlying charter agreement; (4) SEPA CT (SEPA Credit Transfer) for euro settlements within Switzerland and the EEA, using the deep SEPA scheme to transfer funds directly to EU freight forwarders. For recurring payroll and contractor payments, execution via SWIFT Plus or the bank's file-transmission command (e.g., EBICS) is recommended. All outbound disbursements must maintain a contemporaneous audit trail comprising purchase orders, serverless invoices, certificate of flight operations, and the issuance of an authorization notification to the legal, compliance, and treasury mailbox.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla currency forwards on CHF/EUR/USD up to 12-month tenor, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or IFEMA
Currency options (European style) on CHF/USD and CHF/EUR for ticket price stabilization in cargo charter contracts
Cross-currency swaps for converting long-term USD receivables into CHF funding flows, governed by an ISDA and CSA
Financing-style FX swaps with the treasury bank for short-term liquidity alignment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and Federal Direct Corporate Income & Capital Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) jointly with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date; cantonal extensions generally grant filing by 30 September of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest at 5% per annum; procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; tax evasion penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax and criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss Value Added Tax Return (Mehrwertsteuererklärung/Déclaration TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly periods due within 60 days after quarter end; annual filing period may be authorised by ESTV for small taxpayers, with annual return due 60 days after 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on late VAT at 5% per annum; administrative fine up to twice the tax deficiency in aggravated cases; criminal penalty in fraudulent cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 March of the following calendar year; nil declarations accepted for periods with no taxable distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing violation under Art. 62 of the Withholding Tax Act; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000; late interest at 5% per annum

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Social Security Wage Statement (AHV/Lohnbescheinigungen)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) on behalf of the Federal Old-Age, Survivors' and Invalidity Insurance administration (BSV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final annual contribution declaration and wage lists due by 31 January of the following year; contribution advances payable quarterly within 30 days after quarter end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties under Art. 23 AHVG up to CHF 10,000; recovery of arrears plus interest; criminal sanction for wilful wage concealment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Notification of UBO or Shareholding Control Changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); UBO data transmitted to the Federal Office of Justice central register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of a binding resolution or effective change in directors, share transfer creating UBO change, or other registrable fact; no annual renewal filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directory penalty and court-ordered compliance; false certification triggers criminal liability under Swiss Criminal Code; potential administrative fines for breach of registration duty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; minutes retained in corporate minute book (no statutory filing to the commercial register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance sheet date under Art. 699 para 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability for failure to convene; shareholder right to petition the court for convocation at company expense; repeated default may lead to court-ordered dissolution under Art. 731b CO

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Simplified statutory audit (eingeschränkte Revision) is mandatory if the company exceeds two of three thresholds in two consecutive years: CHF 1,000,000 total assets; CHF 2,000,000 turnover; 10 full-time employees. Ordinary statutory audit (ordentliche Revision) is required if the company exceeds two of three thresholds in two consecutive years: CHF 20,000,000 total assets; CHF 40,000,000 turnover; 250 full-time employees, or if it is listed or has outstanding bonds. Small AGs not exceeding the simplified-audit thresholds may opt out by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), which constitutes Swiss statutory accounting law; voluntary adoption of Swiss GAAP FER, IFRS, or US GAAP is permitted for additional reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing to a public register. The AG must maintain a current share and UBO record; any shareholding transfer or change of ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported to the Cantonal Commercial Register within 30 days. The board confirms the accuracy of the share register and UBO data at the annual general meeting, and this confirmation is minuted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (General Meeting and Board Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 2,500 per year (CHF 500 - 2,500) for Swiss registered office administration and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 6,000 per year (CHF 1,800 - 5,500) depending on audit scope, group structure, and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal, cantonal and communal headline rate of approximately 11.5%–21.2% depending on canton; the Swiss federal component is a flat 8.5% on post-tax profit (approximately 7.83% pre-tax), with the Zug ordinary full-tax regime yielding approximately 11.5% effective combined liability for an AG engaged in air cargo brokerage.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory patent box regime excluding up to 90% of qualifying Swiss-related IP income; research and development super-deduction of up to 150% of eligible R&D costs; notional interest deduction (NID) on excess taxable equity; Swiss participation relief of 100% on qualifying substantial dividend income and capital gains; holding-privilege tax transparency on qualifying participations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official cantonal corporate income-and-capital tax return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale personnes morales), filed electronically through the cantonal eTax portal (e.g., eTax Zug) or the Swiss federal EasyGov/eTax filing access points; supplementary form for federal direct tax (Bundessteuer) consolidates federal and cantonal assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the tax return must generally be filed by 31 March of the year following the tax period; Swiss cantonal authorities routinely grant extensions to 30 June upon request. Under Art. 124-125 of the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act (DBG), the taxpayer is under a duty to file once the cantonal forms are issued, and failure to respect the final deadline triggers default assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement net profit/loss for the financial year as per statutory Swiss GAAP or IFRS accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG wholly owned by non-residents, enter the Swiss statutory annual net result after depreciation and reserves; no imputation or branch-level streaming applies at federal level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1.2 - Taxable equity and capital certificate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-relevant paid-in share capital and retained earnings subject to Swiss cantonal capital tax and federal issuance duty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxed directly on the AG's retained income; the AG itself is the taxable entity under Swiss entity-level taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtraction of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from substantial participations under Art. 69-70 DBG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provides a 100% exclusion on qualifying intra-group or portfolio dividends; non-resident control does not affect availability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unused tax loss carry-forward from prior periods, limited to a 7-year statutory window under Art. 67 DBG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry-forward utilization is computed against the entire Swiss taxable income; no foreign entity percentage limitation beyond the participation and ownership thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Violation of procedural filing duties: fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG; default assessment at the tax authority's discretion with 4.5% per annum late-payment interest (Art. 170 DBG); repeated non-compliance may trigger criminal prosecution of the responsible director and additional cantonal surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions from a Swiss AG to shareholders, including non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For non-resident shareholders, treaty relief is implemented by an ex-post refund procedure: the Swiss AG withholds the 35%, the non-resident recipient files Form R-106/R-107 refund application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), attaching a valid official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's state of residence. Where the applicable double tax agreement (DTA) provides a reduced rate (commonly 0%, 5%, 15% depending on shareholding percentage, holding period, and active business conduct), ESTV refunds the differential; beneficial-ownership, substance and anti-abuse clauses must be satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under Swiss domestic law and 0% under the vast majority of Swiss DTAs for payments of IP royalties, including payments from a Swiss air-cargo broker to foreign licensors. Interest: 0% domestic Swiss withholding tax on ordinary direct intra-group and third-party loan interest; however, a 35% Swiss WHT applies to interest paid on publicly issued bonds, book-entry bonds and intermediated securities; treaty rates typically reduce this to 0%-10% depending on the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss CbCR is mandatory for group revenue of at least CHF 900 million (approximately EUR 750 million); Switzerland does not impose statutory Local File or Master File thresholds in the form of fixed amounts, but under Art. 57 DBG and OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, adequate contemporaneous documentation must be available and supplied on Swiss tax audit request for all cross-border related-party transactions, including air-cargo charter fees, fuel surcharges, and handling commissions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, Swiss corporate and tax law impose an economic-substance benchmark through Art. 50 DBG (effective seat and actual administration in Switzerland), the Swiss Criminal Code prohibition of sham transactions, and the tax treaty beneficial-ownership and LOB principles. For the air-cargo charter broker AG, the Swiss tax administration expects physical office presence, meaningful managerial decision-making in Switzerland, sufficient operational staff, genuine commercial activity in charter brokering, and locally maintained books and records; a pure letter-box company with no operational substance is exposed to retroactive denial of DTA relief and anti-avoidance reassessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of false charter invoices, backdated freight agreements, fictitious fuel surcharge rebates, or falsified ledger entries to divert Swiss-source air-cargo brokerage income to non-resident shell entities while filing a knowingly incorrect Swiss corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 176 DBG (Steuerbetrug), conviction carries imprisonment of up to 6 months and a fine; under Art. 175 DBG, simple tax evasion is fined up to 3 times the evaded tax, plus the evaded tax itself and 4.5% annual interest; supplementary Federal Act penalties may apply for customs-duty or VAT-related fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally prosecuted personally, face pre-trial detention and international travel bans in mutual legal assistance proceedings, be held civilly liable under Art. 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations for restitution of the company's tax losses, and be disqualified from board service; where forged corporate certifications are involved, directors may face imprisonment of up to 5 years under Art. 251 StGB.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Swiss AG as a bare invoicing conduit for air-cargo charter transactions, with no salaried staff, no board decisions in Switzerland, no Swiss bank activity, and all risk and control functions residing in the foreign ultimate parent or in the ultimate beneficial owner's home jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty withholding tax relief; retroactive imposition of 35% dividend/interest or royalty Swiss levy where applicable; reassessment of taxable Swiss profits with penalties; Swiss anti-avoidance principles permit annulment of abusive structures; use of the conduit may also trigger the Estonian/VAT base harmonization, where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be regarded as day-to-day executive officers and assessed personally for penalties; civil restitution claims may be brought by the Swiss tax administration against trustees and board members who advanced the sham; criminal proceedings under StGB Art. 251 and 305bis may lead to travel bans and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Air-cargo brokerage funds received from unexplained sources, layered through multiple Swiss AG bank accounts via staggered discount invoices, quick-turnaround charters, over-invoicing of freight handling, or conversion into cryptoassets; failure to conduct the statutory AML due diligence required of licensed charter-broker and payment service intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis StGB imposes up to 3 years imprisonment or a monetary penalty for intentional money laundering; negligent conduct is punishable by a fine of up to CHF 500,000 under Art. 305ter StGB; assets derived from the offense are confiscated under Art. 70 StGB; FINMA or the Swiss AML authority may impose cease-and-desist orders and license revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally exposed as principals or accomplices, may be subject to immediate provisional detention and travel bans, personal bank accounts may be frozen, and private assets may be confiscated; the financial supervisory sanction may include disqualification from managing any Swiss licensed entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Artificial Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividend repatriation as purchase-price payments, management fees, fictitious interest, tacit profit-sharing payments, or share buy-backs, or otherwise failing to withhold the 35% Swiss federal WHT on distributions from the AG to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss Verrechnungssteuergesetz (VStG) requires the AG to pay the 35% WHT to ESTV; non-withheld amounts are collected retroactively with 4.5% annual interest; criminal sanctions include fines and imprisonment under Art. 44-46 VStG for willful dangerous actions, plus an administrative fine of up to three times the unpaid WHT in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing officers who order or implement artificial distributions are jointly and severally liable to ESTV for uncleared WHT and interest; the corporate veil is pierced where the distribution was made in the personal interest of the directors or UBO, leading to civil restitution, asset freezing, travel bans, and imprisonment in aggravated fraudulent cases.
